repealed_predecessor.note_ar: المادة الثلاثون تنص صراحة على أن هذا النظام يحل محل نظام جباية أموال الدولة الصادر بالإرادة الملكية رقم (41/3/2) وتاريخ 12/4/1359هـ (المبلغ بالأمر السامي رقم 5732 في 4/5/1359هـ)، ويلغي كل ما يتعارض معه من أحكام.

verification_methodology_note: PRIMARY SOURCES: this track's text rests on THREE independent sources in agreement: (1) laws.boe.gov.sa (Bureau of Experts / BOE portal), lawId 8b100aee-54a5-48c1-9866-a9a700f2d539 — the live LawDetails and Viewer pages both returned HTTP 503 on direct fetch, so the portal was reached via the Internet Archive Wayback Machine (LawDetails snapshot timestamp 20260215022243, fetched over HTTPS with the environment's proxy CA bundle after a plain-curl attempt without the bundle was blocked by egress policy); this snapshot embeds the FULL Arabic text of all 31 articles plus Article 28-bis, the Royal Decree and Council of Ministers Resolution preambles verbatim, and per-article amendment-history ('تعديلات المادة') popups for the two amended/added articles. (2) nezams.com, fetched directly (HTTP 200), independently confirming the decree/resolution numbers and dates, the 32-item article count (31 numbered + Article 28-bis) shown in its own article navigation menu, and reproducing Article 25's amendment note and Article 28-bis's substantive text word-for-word identically to BOE (though it names a DIFFERENT instrument for the latter — see known_unresolved_discrepancies). (3) qanoonsa.com, reached via search-engine-indexed snippets only (not a direct full-page fetch this pass), corroborating Royal Decree M/68 dated 18/11/1431H as the law's issuing instrument. All 32 records (31 numbered articles + Article 28-bis) are cross-verified from at least two of these three sources in full agreement on substantive text; the decree/resolution citation is confirmed by all three. STRUCTURE: this law has NO formal فصل (chapter) subdivisions in BOE's own markup — see known_unresolved_discrepancies. AMENDMENTS: Article 25 was amended by Royal Decree M/5 (2/1/1440H), deleting the phrase 'أو تقسيط' and rephrasing the article; this is a CORRECTION/ADDITION relative to the prior unverified research lead, which mentioned only Royal Decree M/93 (1443H) as an amending instrument and did not mention M/5 at all. Article 28-bis (المادة الثامنة والعشرون مكرر) was added — confirmed genuine and its full text recovered — with BOE citing Royal Decree M/93 (1/10/1443H) as the adding instrument (nezams.com disagrees on the instrument; see known_unresolved_discrepancies). No other articles show 'changed-article' CSS markup, 'تعديلات المادة' changelog sections, or 'أضيفت'/'عدلت' language in either BOE's or nezams.com's rendering; the remaining 29 numbered articles (1-24, 26-28, 29-31) are therefore treated as اصلية (original, unamended) with no history entries. REPEAL: Article 30 confirms this law repeals its predecessor, نظام جباية أموال الدولة (Royal Will 41/3/2, 12/4/1359H). SCOPE EXCLUSION: a July-2026 Council of Ministers approval of an 'updated' version of this law is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from this track as genuinely unconfirmed (no promulgating instrument number found) — see known_unresolved_discrepancies for the full disclosure. This track represents Royal Decree M/68 (1431H) as amended by M/5 (1440H) and M/93 (1443H) — the pre-2026-update, currently-in-force consolidated text.

known_unresolved_discrepancies.description: The prior unverified research lead stated that Royal Decree M/68 was 'dated 17/11/1431H, approved via Council of Ministers Resolution No. 359 the same date' — this is corrected by direct primary-source verification. laws.boe.gov.sa's own LawDetails page (fetched via the Wayback Machine, snapshot timestamp 20260215022243, over HTTPS with the proxy CA bundle after a direct fetch returned HTTP 503), nezams.com, and qanoonsa.com all independently agree: Royal Decree M/68 is dated 18/11/1431H (26/10/2010G), and Council of Ministers Resolution No. 359 is dated 17/11/1431H — one day EARLIER than the decree, not the same date. The decree's own preamble explicitly cites the Resolution as a preceding instrument ('بعد الاطلاع على قرار مجلس الوزراء رقم (359) وتاريخ 17/11/1431هـ'), consistent with the normal resolution-then-decree sequence. Three independent sources agree on the corrected dates; none support the original lead's claim of an identical date.

Confirmed instance of this corpus's well-documented BOE pattern: the portal's default/main-body text for Article 25 is STALE (pre-amendment), retaining the phrase 'أو تقسيط' ('or installment'), while BOE's own per-article amendment-history ('تعديلات المادة') entry for the SAME article gives the current post-amendment text with the phrase removed, attributing the change to Royal Decree M/5 dated 2/1/1440H. nezams.com independently shows the identical split (stale main-body text + the same M/5 changelog note, word for word), which corroborates both the original 1431H wording and the current wording with two independent sources in full agreement. This track uses the changelog's post-amendment text as the governing current text (article_text_verified) and preserves the stale main-body wording verbatim in original_1431h_text — this is one of the few articles in this corpus where BOTH the original and current wording are recovered to primary-source confidence, not a documented gap.

Article 28-bis (المادة الثامنة والعشرون مكرر) genuinely exists and its substantive text is identical, word for word, across BOE and nezams.com. However, the two sources disagree on which instrument added it: BOE's own per-article history attributes it to Royal Decree M/93 dated 1/10/1443H; nezams.com attributes the identical text to Council of Ministers Resolution No. 198 dated 4/4/1443H — about six months earlier, and a different instrument TYPE (Council resolution vs. Royal Decree), not just a differing date on the same instrument (contrast with the Income Tax Law track's Article 66, where both sources at least agreed it was Royal Decree M/52 and only the day/month of that same decree was disputed). One plausible reading — NOT confirmed this pass — is that Resolution 198 was the Council's internal approval and M/93 was the later Royal Decree that formally promulgated it (mirroring the Resolution-359-then-Decree-M/68 sequence for the original 1431H law, only with a much longer gap). A web search for uqn.gov.sa's own Umm Al-Qura Gazette page for M/93 (https://uqn.gov.sa/?p=13146) returned HTTP 503 on the only attempt made this pass and was not independently confirmed. Per this corpus's zero-guessing policy, this track cites BOE's attribution (Royal Decree M/93, 1/10/1443H) as the primary record — consistent with BOE serving as the base/primary source elsewhere in this corpus — while recording nezams.com's conflicting attribution verbatim in the article's own amendment_history rather than silently discarding it.

Unlike this corpus's other fiscal-law tracks (income_tax_law, vat_law, zakat_law), the State Revenue Law has NO formal فصل (chapter) subdivisions in BOE's own structural markup — the HTML contains no chapter-title elements, only a flat sequence of 31 numbered articles plus Article 28-bis. BOE's descriptive 'نبذة عن النظام' summary lists topical themes in prose (definitions, general provisions, revenue estimation, collection, seizure/enforcement, debt exemption/installment, closing provisions) but these are NOT formal numbered فصول with their own headers, and no chapter_structure array is populated in this track's source artifact for that reason — a confirmed structural fact, not an omission.

A SEPARATE, more recent development exists and must not be conflated with this track: on Tuesday 14 July 2026 (per aawsat.com, confirmed independently by sabq.org and referenced in web-search snippets of qanoonsa.com), the Saudi Council of Ministers approved an 'updated' State Revenue Law (نظام إيرادات الدولة المحدث) during a session in Jeddah, with Finance Minister Mohammed Al-Jadaan thanking the leadership for its approval. NEITHER aawsat.com NOR sabq.org names any Royal Decree number, Council of Ministers Resolution number, or other promulgating-instrument identifier for this update, and neither states whether it has been published in the Official Gazette or entered into force. As of this research pass, this update remains GENUINELY UNCONFIRMED as to its exact citation and legal effect. This track deliberately represents only the pre-2026-update, currently-in-force text (M/68 as amended by M/5 and M/93) and explicitly excludes the unconfirmed 2026 update. No firm decree/resolution number for the 2026 update was found anywhere in this research pass to report.
